name: FAIR Universe HiggsML Uncertainty Challenge
description: Develop machine learning models to estimate the signal strength parameter (µ) and provide a 68.27% Confidence Interval (CI), accounting for both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties. The task involves systematic biases introduced by six nuisance parameters to simulate real-world uncertainties.

cr:input.name: FAIR Universe HiggsML Uncertainty Dataset
cr:input.description: Tabular dataset in parquet format containing simulated proton-proton collision events. Features include raw measurements (e.g., PRI_had_pt, PRI_lep_eta, PRI_met) and derived features (e.g., DER_mass_transverse_met_lep, DER_deltaeta_jet_jet). Labels include binary classification (1 for signal, 0 for background). Systematic biases are introduced via six nuisance parameters (e.g., αtes, αjes).

cr:output.name: predictions
cr:output.description: Predicted 68.27% Confidence Interval (CI) bounds for the signal strength parameter (µ). Output includes lower bound (µ16) and upper bound (µ84), clipped to a maximum value of 3.

field.name: mu_16
field.description: Lower bound of the 68.27% Confidence Interval for µ. Example: 0.5.

field.name: mu_84
field.description: Upper bound of the 68.27% Confidence Interval for µ. Example: 1.5.

cr:evaluation.notes: The final quantile score is computed as -ln((w + ε)f(c)), where ε = 10^-2 and f(c) is an asymmetric penalty function penalizing deviations from 68.27% coverage.
